newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians vow more protests over pyramid schemes.
newsitem.headline: Albanians vow more protests over pyramid schemes.

text.p: Enraged Albanians who lost their savings in pyramid schemes vowed to stage further protests on Saturday against the Balkan country's rightist government after setting a town hall ablaze.

"We will do the same thing again tomorrow," one protester shouted at reporters on Friday in the town of Lushnje 85 km (55 miles) southwest of Tirana. "We will block the road and if police come we will fight them as we did today."

Opposition parties blame the government for failing to prevent the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes which created false hopes among the citizens of what is Europe's poorest country and are demanding fresh elections.
The opposition alleges the ruling Democrats financed their election campaign in a municipal poll in October through pyramid schemes -- a charge the government has denied.
Eyewitnesses said they saw several truckloads of police reinforcements heading towards Lushnje on Friday night.
Supporters of the town's soccer club, owned by the promoter of one of the pyramid schemes, said they would travel to the nearby town of Fieri to persuade residents there to join the protest.
The leftist opposition is planning a mass protest in Tirana on Sunday.
Friday's disturbance was the latest in a series by desperate savers who lost what little they had accumulated since the fall of communism in Europe's poorest country.

Many hold President Sali Berisha's government responsible for their losses. One opposition party said it would call for fresh protests next week if ministers did not explain clearly how consumers would be compensated.
Berisha told a television interviewer that he understood the fury of impoverished Albanians and promised that they would get back pyramid scheme money now frozen in bank accounts.

"Let people be assured that the money seized in the banks is theirs and we will give it back to them with interest," he said. But he accused opposition parties of trying to exploit savers' misfortune.
About 5,000 people massed in front of Lushnje town hall on Friday, smashing windows, setting a police truck on fire and pelting riot police with rocks.
They later set the building ablaze and ransacked a cinema before dispersing. Twelve police were taken to hospital, two in serious condition.
The protest in Lushnje was the most violent to date. About 1,000 demonstrators also massed on Friday southwest of Tirana in Kavaje, Berisha's political stronghold.
The government last week set up a commission to investigate the dubious investment schemes and froze 25.5 billion leks ($25.5 million) deposited by some schemes in state banks.
Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi said the government would submit a law to parliament next week setting down how to reimburse investors.
Parliament, controlled by Berisha's Democratic Party, banned the schemes in a bid to end the protests. The law also warned operators they could face up to 20 years in jail.
The official ATA news agency said on Friday that a Tirana court had upheld the arrest of the managers of two schemes on embezzlement charges.
One company, Gjallica, has filed for bankruptcy, which could trigger more protests. Thousands last week besieged the city hall in the western town of Vlore, where Gjallica has its head office.
